about: Eguren Ugarte is a family winery in Páganos, a hamlet of the walled medieval town of Laguardia in Rioja Alavesa. The family’s story in wine begins in 1870, when Anastasio Eguren, a chocolate merchant from Bergara, settled in the Sonsierra after marrying; his son Trifón began the winemaking line. Six generations on, the estate is run by Asun and Mercedes Eguren, daughters of Victorino Eguren Ugarte, the man who turned a family vineyard into a modern bodega with two kilometres of underground cellars and a hotel among the vines.

The family farms more than 130 hectares in Rioja Alavesa, some of it over a century old, on clay-limestone soils between about 400 and 700 metres. The Sierra de Cantabria rises behind the vineyards, sheltering them from cold northern winds, while the climate blends Mediterranean warmth with Atlantic freshness. The Reserva is built on Tempranillo with a small share of Graciano, the traditional Rioja partner that adds colour, acidity and lift. As a Rioja Reserva it must be aged at least three years before release, at least one of them in oak barrels.

The winery describes the 2017 as bright cherry red, with aromas of ripe fruit, licorice and vanilla, a balanced palate and a gently sweet, fruity finish. James Suckling found dusty spice with cherry and berry fruit, hints of nougat and pine cone, and a medium body, and suggested it would show best from 2025 onward.
facts: Rioja Reserva (minimum three years’ aging, at least one in barrel)
